# Adopt v1.4.0

This release adds a palette-independent Graphite icon treatment and a live app preview on the Reference's Colors tab. Existing semantic theme roles, accent palettes, surface tones, typography, geometry and supported runtimes are unchanged. If upgrading from before v1.3.0, also follow [the v1.3.0 migration](v1.3.0.md).

## Pin the release

Update the immutable dependency, lockfile and consumer manifest together. Use the public v1.4.0 GitHub tag for CSS/assets/commands and the exact 1.4.0 Swift Package Manager version. Verify the public tag before changing a consumer pin. See [the release process](../releases.md) for channel verification; a source version does not prove publication.

## Graphite icons

The recommended background is a two-stop monochrome gradient from #383838 at the top left to #202020 at the bottom right, with the existing #F5F5F5 foreground. It stays neutral across all interface accents. Preserve each product's identifying glyph, use its 16px drawing when available, regenerate the platform exports, and refresh cached favicon URLs.

Start with [the monochrome base](../../assets/app-icon-monochrome-base.svg). Canonical values live in `icon.monochromeGradient`; generated CSS exposes `--icon-monochrome-gradient`. Swift exposes `AppStylrTokens.Icon.monochromeGradientStops` and `monochromeGradientAngleDegrees`:

```swift
LinearGradient(
  stops: AppStylrTokens.Icon.monochromeGradientStops,
  startPoint: .topLeading,
  endPoint: .bottomTrailing
)
```

The solid base, `icon.background` fallback, and original colored gradient asset/values remain available. No existing token or asset is renamed or repurposed. See [platform icon guidance](../platform-icons.md) for generation and actual-size review.

## Reference hosting

The Colors tab now shows the selected appearance in an interactive project-workspace specimen. Palette cards and global appearance controls drive the same preview; form and row interactions remain local to the specimen. This demonstrates role relationships and responsive behavior, not a required application layout.

Rebuild the portable Reference from the new package and deploy its entire artifact. Root and subpath hosts retain their existing URL and asset behavior. Verify the version manifest, favicon cache key, monochrome-base download and Colors preview at desktop and phone widths.
